name: Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)
overview: In the majority in the Lembe-Yezoum subdivision, the Yezoum, who came from Adamawa, live alongside the Vute, Yebekolo, Nanga, Mvele, Eton and Mbamois. Their dynastic chiefdom is held by the great Angoula family. Trade, cash and food crops, basketry and the making of musical instruments provide their living; their culture and language are close to those of the Ewondo.

sections.title: Identity and neighbours
items: Majority group in its district, in contact with the Vute, Yebekolo, Nanga, Mvele, Eton and Mbamois.
Yezoum live in the Centre, the South, the East, and beyond; all consider themselves relatives.
Mainly indigenous group, but marriages are now mostly exogamous.

sections.title: Territory and migrations
items: The present lands were occupied by the Yebekolo, who were pushed back further into Haute-Sanaga.
The group came from Adamawa.

sections.title: Social organisation and power
items: The chief is master of the lands, people and property; the chiefdom is a dynasty held by the Angoula family, where the throne passes from father to son.
Everybody can express themselves in public in the face of a serious problem.
Formerly, the successor redistributed the inheritance to his brothers and sisters; today, the will is followed.
Land conflicts occur almost every year.
The wife owes obedience to her husband, children owe respect to adults.

sections.title: Kinship, marriage and life passages
items: Patrilineal kinship: the family tree follows the man's line. The wife joins her husband's family.
A boy becomes a man at around 18, with fields, a house and a wife.
Three essential stages: marriage proposal, engagement, bride price.
Bride price: wrappers and large cooking pots for the mothers, wine for the fathers, in recognition of the care given to the young woman.

sections.title: Beliefs, sacred places and taboos
items: Akɔg Mfila, a cave in the Ebɔlboumou area, is a place of contemplation and prayer.
Death takes one back to the forebears.
Taboos: vulgar language and talking about sexuality in public.
Taboos: women eat neither gorilla, nor chimpanzee, nor certain game; a boy eats snake only if a parent gives it to him.
Capital offences: incest and raising a hand against one's parents or elders.

sections.title: Economy, land and crafts
items: All take part in trade, cash crops and subsistence farming.
All the land belongs to the chief.
Crafts: basketry (food bags, carrying baskets for tubers), chairs, musical instruments (balafon, tam-tam, drum).

sections.title: Clothing, health, beauty
items: Formerly, men and women wore clothes made of animal skins.
Most people today are treated at the hospital, considered safer.
Beauty: talent for the man; the hard-working woman, a good cook and good housekeeper.

sections.title: Music, dances and festivals
items: Instruments made locally: balafon, tam-tam, drum.

sections.title: History and cultural kinship
items: Way of life, culture and language bring the Yezoum close to the Ewondo.

sections.title: The names
items: There are men's names and women's names, but no twin names.
In princely families, the father proposed a name to the family, which deliberated for nine days; the name does not change.
Appellative a-: a-Mvoto.
Si-məkɔɔ, one of the ancestors, was the 20th king of the chiefdom.

lessons.title: Who are the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)? Identity, language and territory
objectives: Name the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community and explain its name
Locating your territory and its neighbours
Telling one's origin according to tradition
lessons.competence: Introduce the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.
lessons.situation: A pen pal from another region asks you to introduce the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community to them: who are they, where do they live, where do they come from?
lessons.materiel: Map of Cameroon, cultural profile of the community (“Cultures” section of Likalo).

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Present the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within Cameroon's cultural diversity.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read: “A pen friend from another region asks you to introduce the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community to them: who are they, where do they live, where do they come from?” The students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What do the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) call themselves and what does this name mean? — What language do they speak, and where else is it spoken? — Which peoples do they live with? — Where did they come from, according to tradition?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Group in the majority in its arrondissement, in contact with the Vute, Yebekolo, Nanga, Mvele, Eton and Mbamois. • Yezoum live in the Centre, the South, the East, and beyond; all consider themselves relatives. • Mostly indigenous group, but marriages are now mainly exogamous. • The present lands were occupied by the Yebekolo, who were pushed back further into Haute-Sanaga. • The group came from Adamawa.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: In the majority in the Lembe-Yezoum subdivision, the Yezoum, who came from Adamawa, live alongside the Vute, Yebekolo, Nanga, Mvele, Eton and Mbamois. Their dynastic chiefdom is held by the great Angoula family. Trade, cash and food crops, basketry and the making of musical instruments provide their living; their culture and language are close to those of the Ewondo.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: On a map of Cameroon, locate the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) community and its neighbours, then write 5 sentences to introduce it to your pen pal.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.title: Power and social organisation among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)

lessons.competence: Describe how the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-II — Cultural practices: ways of life
lessons.title: Traditional food and drink of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)
objectives: Linking food to the living environment
lessons.competence: Identify the traditional dishes and drinks of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), describe how they are prepared and bring out their cultural significance.
lessons.situation: Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group must present a traditional dish of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum).
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile, pictures or local ingredients, display materials.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Identify the traditional foods and drinks of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), describe their preparation and bring out their cultural significance.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read: “Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group has to present a traditional dish of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum).” The students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the main dishes and drinks? — What products are they made from? Where do these products come from? — Who prepares them, and on what occasions? — What do they say about the community's living environment?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Traditional dishes: groundnut sauce, groundnut dishes, cassava leaves (kpəm). • Drinks: palm wine, raffia wine. • Everyone takes part in trade, cash crops and food farming.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) mainly eat groundnut sauce, groundnut dishes, kpəm. Traditional drinks: palm wine, raffia wine. These dishes are linked to the group's activities and to the products of its environment.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Choose a dish of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum): write its sheet (name in the language, ingredients, steps, occasion when it is served).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.memo: Among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), dances accompany the great moments of life: celebrations, mourning, weddings, initiations. Instruments: balafon, tam-tam, drum.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-IV — Cultural practices in communities (Level I)
lessons.title: Traditional economy and access to land among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)
lessons.competence: Describe the economic activities of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.
lessons.situation: A development project wants to help the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). First it must understand how they work and who owns the land.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the economic activities of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read: “A development project wants to help the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). First it must understand how they work and who owns the land.” The students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the activities of men? of women? — Who owns the land and how is it accessed? — Which products are sold or exchanged? — Have these activities changed?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Everyone takes part in trade, cash crops and food farming. • All the land belongs to the chief. • Crafts: basketry (bags for foodstuffs, baskets for tubers), chairs, musical instruments (balafon, tam-tam, drum).

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Everyone takes part in trade, cash crops and subsistence farming. All the land belongs to the chief.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Draw a two-column table (men / women) of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)'s activities, then explain how land is accessed.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Beliefs, sacred places and taboos among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum)
objectives: Explain beliefs about life and death
lessons.competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), and their role in regulating social life.
lessons.situation: A visitor arrives among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). Which places and which rules must he absolutely respect?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum), and their role in regulating social life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read: “A visitor arrives among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). Which places and which rules must they absolutely respect?” The students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the beliefs about birth and death? — Which places are sacred, and why? — What are the main taboos, and for whom? — How were serious offences atoned for?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following elements: • Akɔg Mfila, a cave in the Ebɔlboumou area, is a place of contemplation and prayer. • Death brings people back to the ancestors. • Taboos: vulgarity and talking about sexuality in public. • Prohibitions: women do not eat gorilla, chimpanzee or certain game; a boy eats snake only if a parent gives it to him. • Capital offences: incest and raising a hand against one's parents or elders.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Akɔg Mfila, a cave in the Ebɔlboumou area, is a place of contemplation and prayer. Death brings one back to the ancestors.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Write a short guide to good conduct for a visitor among the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) (3 places or rules to respect, with their reason).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and counting in Yezoum
lessons.anelcac: Traditional media and transmission: everyday language
objectives: Greeting according to the time of day
lessons.competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.
lessons.situation: You are visiting a Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) family. Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in the sharing of kola nuts by counting.
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile (“Common expressions” and “Counting” sections), kola nuts or small objects.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Use the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) greeting and introduction formulas and count from 1 to 10, respecting customary usage.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read: “You are visiting a Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum) family. Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in the sharing of the cola nuts by counting.” The students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How do you greet people depending on the time of day? — How do you introduce yourself (name, origin, place of residence)? — How do you count from 1 to 10? Is the system decimal, vigesimal…? — Why is language a tool of transmission?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • The community's language is Yezoum. • Greetings: Mbolo = Hello (neutral greeting, at any time of day); Mbəmbə atié = morning greeting (one person); Mbəmbə atié = morning greeting (several people). • Counting from 1 to 5: Fɔɔ, Bɛɛ, Lɛ, Ŋi, Tan. • Si-məkɔɔ, one of the ancestors, was the 20th king of the chiefdom. • Way of life, culture and language bring the Yezoum close to the Ewondo.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Greeting and counting in Yezoum are the first steps towards communicating with the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). Polite formulas express the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Role play in pairs: greet each other, introduce yourselves, ask where the other person comes from and count objects from 1 to 10.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.intro: Learn to greet, introduce yourself and count in Yezoum.

activities.title: I greet
activities.instruction: Learn the greeting formulas for morning, midday and evening.

activities.title: I introduce myself
activities.instruction: Say your name, where you are from and where you live.

activities.title: I count
activities.instruction: Count objects from 1 to 10.

activities.title: I pass on
activities.instruction: Teach a formula to a classmate or a family member.

student.memo: Greeting and counting in Yezoum are the first steps towards communicating with the Yezoum (Lembe-Yezoum). Polite formulas express the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.
